summary: Marache Point light at the south entrance to Arichat Harbour, Isle Madame, has shown a light since 1851; its 1949 lighthouse gave way to a modular tower in 2018.

structures.note: Lighthouse with living space, built under contract for $1,395 (Lighthouse Friends). The sources read do not give its material.
New lighthouse with dwelling, boathouse and storehouse (Lighthouse Friends, Isle Madame Lighthouses).

structures.type: square tower, white with a red upper portion
structures.note: Modular, aluminum-framed building brought in by road in January 2018 (Isle Madame Lighthouses); height from the Coast Guard's List of Lights.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed. The last stretch must be walked because a bridge has been removed (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Local interests permitted to establish a beacon light on Marache Point.
Beacon lit with Joseph DeCoste as first keeper; no dwelling at the light.
New lighthouse with living space, under contract for $1,395, placed in operation 1 October 1869.
270-degree fifth-order dioptric apparatus replaced the lamps and reflectors. The Department's report for fiscal 1909-10 lists it as an Arichat improvement; the NSLPS list gives 1922.
New lighthouse with dwelling, boathouse and storehouse built.
Commercial power extended to the station.
Light destaffed; battery-powered system for power failures; other station buildings declared surplus and sold. NSLPS gives automation by 1973.
Name officially changed from Arichat Lighthouse to Marache Point Lighthouse, a few months after automation.
Residents approved the Coast Guard proposal to replace the lighthouse at a public meeting in Arichat, 3 October 2017.
Modular, aluminum-framed building brought in by road in January 2018.

corrections.why: The tower standing since January 2018 is a modular, aluminum-framed building (Isle Madame Lighthouses). The wooden tower of 1949 was replaced in 2018.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends gives 1909 for the fifth-order lens, and the Department's report for fiscal 1909-10 records the substitution under the heading 'Arichat, Canso Harbour'. The NSLPS light table gives 1922, later than the Department's report. The story states both.

notes_for_editor: Checked 2026-10-28 against the sources. Lighthouse Friends' 1909 lens date and the Department's fiscal 1909-10 entry agree; the Department entry is headed 'Arichat, Canso Harbour' (OCR prose, not a table), and the story says so. The identification with Marache Point rests on the Arichat name (Lighthouse Friends: the light was called Arichat Lighthouse until its name was changed) and on the 270-degree fifth-order lens that Lighthouse Friends describes for 1909. Keeper names agree between Lighthouse Friends and Isle Madame Lighthouses apart from spelling (DeCoste/Coste, LaVache/Lavashe, Jeffery/Jeffrey, Micheal/Michael). Isle Madame Lighthouses has 'Joseph Coste 1851 - July 1975' (typo for 1875) and 'In December 2027, the lighthouse was demolished' (typo for 2017); the story relies on neither typo. The NSLPS page gives 'Coste, Joseph' with a 1857 date, which the other two sources do not support. Disagreements stated in the story: lens date (1909 in Lighthouse Friends and the Department; 1922 in the NSLPS light table); automation (1970 destaffed, Lighthouse Friends and Isle Madame; by 1973 and by 1993, NSLPS). 2017 meeting: Lighthouse Friends' account cites The Reporter (12 October 2017), which was not read; the story attributes the meeting to Lighthouse Friends citing that article. Keeper 1877: Lighthouse Friends says 'Keeper DeCoste' in 1877, after Joseph DeCoste's 1875 departure, and does not say which DeCoste; the story keeps that wording. Omitted on purpose: the private names and personal remarks in the Lighthouse Friends account (a relative's comment and the society chair's name), and the commercial app pages that repeat the 2018 date. The 1865 Kendrick inspection and the 1849 Commissioners' remark are known only through Lighthouse Friends' transcriptions; the original Department papers are not in the corpus. The 1911 entry is prose, so no column position was used.
